industry.ipm: Indian domestic formulations market ₹2,565 bn in FY26, +9.9% (IQVIA, as quoted in our Mankind initiation); Q1FY27 IPM +13.0% excl. tirzepatide. Emcure expects industry growth of 8-9% in FY27 (Q4FY26 call)
industry.emcureRank: #13 in the IPM; #2 in gynaecology (8.3% share); #7 in cardiac covered market (19.1% of Emcure's sales); #13 in anti-diabetics (7.9%) (IQVIA MAT Mar-2026)
industry.glp1: Semaglutide's Indian patent expired in Mar-2026; 40-50 generic brands launched (CEO, Aug-2026). Emcure sells Novo Nordisk's rDNA brand Poviztra and cut its price in Apr-2026; two Indian generic makers had recalls (CEO)
industry.inLicensing: MNCs (Sanofi, Novo Nordisk, Roche) increasingly hand Indian brands to local partners with larger field forces; partners earn a distribution margin, not brand ownership. In-licensed products are ~15% of Emcure's India sales
industry.europe: European generics market US$70 bn+; Emcure's priority is complex injectables (liposomal amphotericin B: first EU generic, ~US$270 mn innovator market; ferric carboxymaltose and liposomal doxorubicin next), with own front ends in the UK and Italy and partners elsewhere (Sep-2026 deck)
industry.canada: Marcan is a top-10 generic company in Canada and the largest Indian pharma company by prescriptions; pan-Canadian since Mantra (Quebec); 50+ products in development, 8 near-term first-generic opportunities incl. semaglutide (Sep-2026 deck)
industry.row: ARV (anti-HIV) tenders in Africa and Latin America (donor-funded, lumpy, price-competitive) plus branded non-ARV generics in 80+ countries; voluntary licences for lenacapavir (Gilead) and alimatravir (MSD)

moat.evidence: Orofer XT / FCM lead the iron market (#1 in iron combinations); #2 in gynaecology with 8.3% share; anaemia camps reach 2 lakh women a year

9 chiral molecules (6 first in India), first ferric carboxymaltose in India, in-house biologics (Tenectase 100% share), first EU generic liposomal amphotericin B; ~50% of India revenue from complex products
Sanofi, Novo Nordisk and Roche chose Emcure, but these are distribution rights (Sanofi's initial five years from Mar-2024), not owned brands; they grow with the market
#13 in the IPM with ~4,000 reps; covered-market share and brands per doctor below peers (Kotak question, Aug-2026); India growth at or below the market for two years
Own front ends in Canada (top-10 generic company) and the UK/Italy; but generics in Europe and Canada are price-deflationary and ARV is a tender commodity
Backward-integrated API, 13 Indian plants; EBITDA margin ~19-20% is below India-led peers (25%+) because of the international mix

critiques: India is the weak link: domestic growth was 10% in FY26 and 10.2% in Q1FY27, but only 6-7% excluding the in-licensed Sanofi and Roche brands; Zuventus (40% of the field force) shrank 4% in FY26 and needed a restructuring
Quality of growth: Q1FY27's +22.8% included 6-7pp of currency and ARV tenders at two-thirds of the rest-of-world business; neither is a franchise
Margin structure: gross margin is falling (61.8% → 58.4% in a year) as Europe, ARV and traded in-licensed goods grow; EBITDA margin gains depend on cost control
Working capital: 34% of revenue tied up; operating cash flow was only 53% of EBITDA in FY26, and ₹957 cr went to minority buyouts in ten months

Governance: promoter family runs the company (founder becomes Chairman too; son is COO; daughter and son-in-law in senior roles); ₹276 cr of sales to the promoter-owned US company with ₹197 cr outstanding; a ₹232 cr purchase of Gennova's minority from its CEO at a price ~350x Gennova's FY26 profit
Supply overhang: promoters at 77.8% must sell or dilute ~2.8% to meet the 25% public-float rule

Bull view (MOSL, ICICI Direct): 25% PAT CAGR FY26-28 from operating leverage, niche launches (amphotericin B, semaglutide in Canada, lenacapavir) and a recovering India business; the stock trades at a discount to India-led peers
